absent: Locking, concurrency, and synchronization rules for namespaces, open state, PCI access, and power management.
Function bodies, call sequences, and internal state transitions beyond register and flag definitions.
Allocation, lifetime, ownership, and teardown rules for described records and devices.
Error handling, validation order, and permission checks beyond the retry hint for cached resolution.
Timing, sequencing, and side effects of hotplug events, bridge resets, self test, and power state changes.
Interpretation of spare and reserved fields and version negotiation beyond frozen first sizes.

findings.text: A namespace file handle is a fixed order record holding a wide identifier first, then a narrow type code, then a narrow inode number. The identifier occupies eight bytes while each following field occupies four bytes, giving a compact sixteen byte form in its first published shape.

A namespace identifier request begins with a four byte total size and spare, then an eight byte identifier. It ends with a nested grouping that carries a four byte type plus spare and an eight byte owning user namespace identifier used when listing.

An open configuration record holds three eight byte fields in order for flags, then mode, then path resolution controls. The resolution field selects scoped lookup behaviour while the first two mirror classic open settings in wide form.

Compatibility is preserved by freezing first published sizes. The namespace handle first size stays at sixteen bytes while the latest size follows the current record, and the identifier request first size stays at thirty two bytes while callers advertise their own size in the leading field.

Initial namespace inode numbers occupy the top of the unsigned thirty two bit space and descend by one per type. The IPC initial value is highest at 0xEFFFFFFF, then the UTS value is one lower, then the USER value steps lower again, then PID continues downward, then CGROUP continues downward, then TIME continues downward, then NET continues downward, ending with MNT at 0xEFFFFFF8 plus a kernel only anonymous MNT one step lower.

Initial namespace identifiers are small sequential integers starting at one. IPC uses one, then UTS uses two, then USER uses three, then PID uses four, then CGROUP uses five, then TIME uses six, then NET uses seven, then MNT uses eight which also marks the last initial identifier in kernel builds.

Namespace type codes are single bits matching clone positions. TIME uses bit seven, then MNT uses bit seventeen, then CGROUP uses bit twenty five, then UTS uses bit twenty six, then IPC uses bit twenty seven, then USER uses bit twenty eight, then PID uses bit twenty nine, then NET uses bit thirty.

Two read style namespace operations return an eight byte identifier to callers. One operation retrieves the mount namespace identifier while the other retrieves a generic namespace identifier, each transferring a single unsigned sixty four bit value from kernel to user.
The marker for current user denotes all bits set across sixty four bits and asks list operations to use the caller own user namespace rather than an explicit identifier.

Out of memory scoring uses a signed adjustment span where the minimum marker denotes negative one thousand and the maximum marker denotes positive one thousand. A separate disable marker denotes negative seventeen, while the legacy adjust scale spans from negative sixteen at its minimum to positive fifteen at its maximum.

The regular file flag occupies bit thirty two and limits opening to regular files. Scoping starts with the no cross device marker blocking mount crossings, then the no magic link marker blocking proc style links, then the no symlink marker blocking all symlinks, then the beneath marker confining parent and absolute escapes, then the in root marker re-rooting slash lookups inside the start directory, then the cached marker allowing only cached completion.

A device function code packs slot in five upper bits and function in three lower bits. Construction shifts slot left by three and keeps only low three bits of function, while extraction shifts right and masks for slot and masks directly for function, limiting slot to thirty one and function to seven.

PCI controller operations share a base built from three character codes placed in the high three bytes. Offsets zero through three from that base select controller query and memory map mode for input output space and memory map mode for memory space and write combining control respectively.

Hotplug reporting distinguishes four link and presence conditions. One condition signals link up, another signals link down, another signals card present, and the last signals card absent, allowing listeners to track insertion and link transitions.

Classic configuration space spans two hundred fifty six bytes while extended space spans four thousand ninety six bytes. The standard header itself occupies sixty four bytes and provides six base address registers in normal layouts.

Standard header field positions are fixed. Vendor starts at zero with device at two, then command at four with status at six. Class and revision share offset eight with revision lowest and programming interface middle and device class highest. Cache size sits at twelve with latency at thirteen and header kind at fourteen and self test at fifteen. Interrupt line and pin with minimum grant and maximum latency occupy sixty through sixty three in order.

Command enables occupy low bits of the command halfword. Input output response uses the lowest bit, then memory response uses the next, then mastering follows, then special cycles, then invalidate, then palette snooping, then parity, then stepping, then system error, then fast back to back, then interrupt disable at bit ten.

Status reports readiness, interrupt state, capability presence, bus speed, parity, device select timing, and target and master abort with system error signals. Header kind low bits distinguish normal and bridge and CardBus layouts while the top bit marks multifunction, and self test uses high bits for control with result in the low nibble.

Six base registers start at sixteen and step by four bytes. The lowest bit selects input output versus memory space, with memory type and prefetch flags in low bits and address masks preserving upper bits while clearing flag portions for each space.

Subsystem vendor and identifier follow CardBus information at offsets forty four and forty six, while expansion ROM control sits at forty eight with enable in the lowest bit and address in upper bits. The first capability pointer lives at fifty two and links variable capability structures.

Bridges encode primary, secondary, subordinate bus numbers plus secondary latency in one word at twenty four, then input output and memory and prefetchable windows follow as base and limit pairs with upper half extensions for wide addresses. Companion masks distinguish narrow versus wide window types and alignment.

Bridge control at offset sixty two governs parity and error forwarding and compatibility forwarding plus abort reporting and secondary reset and fast transfers. A header one ROM alias shares the same layout at offset fifty six, while CardBus capability linkage starts at twenty.

CardBus bridges place bus numbers and latency after secondary status, then two memory base limit pairs followed by two input output base limit pairs with high halves. Range masking clears low two bits to align input output windows.

CardBus bridge control mirrors standard controls with added CardBus reset and sixteen bit interrupt plus prefetch and posted write enables. Subsystem vendor and identifier follow at sixty four and sixty six, with legacy sixteen bit base at sixty eight.

Capabilities form a linked list with identifier at zero and next pointer at one and flags at two across four bytes total. Identifiers cover power, graphics, product data, slot, message interrupts, and express through enhanced allocation, with the maximum defined as enhanced allocation.

Power management exposes version, wake, and sleep capabilities plus a control register holding current power state. Devices move among D zero through D three with optional no reset on return from D three hot, while enable and status bits govern wake signalling and data selection scales reported values.

Graphics port capability holds version then status then control. Status advertises request depth, sideband, wide addressing, fast transfers, and rate support, while control enables sideband, overall processing, wide addresses, forced fast transfers, and rate selection.

Vital product data uses a fifteen bit address with completion flag plus a thirty two bit data register in an eight byte capability. Slot identification records expansion slot count and first chassis flag plus chassis number for physical location.

Callers must not assume fixed sizes for versioned namespace records and must use the leading size field with frozen first sizes when exchanging handles across releases. Cached only resolution can fail with retry when entries are absent, and masked PCI fields require read modify write to preserve reserved bits rather than direct writes.
Each user header defines a single inclusion guard macro that prevents repeated inclusion within one translation unit and carries no runtime behaviour.
